tagline: Across a dam that changed both the water and the roads
intro: This drive crosses the West Branch of the Farmington River, rides over Saville Dam and follows the eastern shore of Lake McDonough. The connected sections of routes 181, 318 and 219 are designated scenic roads. Route 318 crosses the top of an earthen embankment with masonry work, 135 feet high and 1,950 feet long.

The Metropolitan District Commission began buying land for the dam and reservoir in 1927. Completed in 1940, Saville Dam created the reservoir that supplies Hartford’s primary water source; filling it took until 1948. The water covered Barkhamsted Hollow and partially flooded Barkhamsted Center.

The reservoir also broke an existing highway connection. Route 181 had originally run east across a road now underwater. It was relocated along the reservoir’s west side, and its separated eastern portion later became part of Route 219. The dam crossing itself entered the state road network before Route 318 existed: SR 418 reached the dam in 1937 and extended across it two years later.

From US 44, follow River Road north into Pleasant Valley and cross the West Branch on the shared stretch of routes 181 and 318. Continue east on 318 over Saville Dam to Route 219, then south along Lake McDonough’s eastern shore toward the East Branch crossing in New Hartford.
notice: Route 318 crosses the dam’s top; its embankment combines earth and masonry.

moments.title: Pleasant Valley
moments.text: Pleasant Valley became Barkhamsted’s civic center after the reservoir displaced the earlier center. The village of Pleasant Valley lies on the west side of the West Branch of the Farmington River. Its town hall and elementary school are among the hamlet’s buildings. Here routes 181 and 318 share the river crossing. Beyond it, East River Road provides access to Peoples State Forest and leads to Riverton. The West Branch is designated a Wild and Scenic River. It runs through both Pleasant Valley and Riverton, and its catch-and-release section hosts anglers year-round.

moments.title: Saville Dam
moments.text: The dam was first known as Bill’s Brook Dam, after a brook near the construction site. In 1940, the Metropolitan District Commission renamed it for its chief engineer, Caleb Mills Saville. Land north of the dam was stripped of lumber and buildings during construction. The structure was completed that May, but Barkhamsted Reservoir did not fill to capacity until 1948. Barkhamsted Hollow’s foundations lie within the reservoir. Route 318 crosses the dam’s top; on the western portion is an uncontrolled spillway. The resulting reservoir impounds the East Branch for nearly eight miles toward Hartland.

moments.title: Lake McDonough
moments.text: Lake McDonough was created to protect downstream mill owners’ water rights. Known as the compensating reservoir, it lies just south of Barkhamsted Reservoir and belongs to the Metropolitan District Commission. The lake now serves recreation, including beaches, boating and fishing. Route 219 follows its eastern shore, with the section between Route 318 and the East Branch of the Farmington River designated scenic.
